text.p: The following are some of the leading stories in Finnish papers this morning.
- Apartment sales increased by one fourth last year and prices rose 4.6 percent in the Helsinki capital area, a Statistics Finland study shows.
- Taxpayers employing "maid help" at home can claim 1,200 markka of expenses in taxes. Maid help is a goverment experiment to cut unemployment. @

- President Martti Ahtisaari signed new law on central bank, increasing its independence and preparing Finland for economic and monetary union (EMU). Law will be implemented at start of next year, but may have to be changed in 1999.
- State-owned companies' profits fell in 1996 by 2.2 billion markka; state owned lottery company Veikkaus Oy was clearly most profitable with return on investments amounting to 88 percent.

- Finnish sporting goods group Amer's Wilson brand tennis rackets have a strong foothold in tennis markets, but new sports have began to erode popularity of tennis, says Wilson sales manager at Amer. @
- All energy options should be open, group of Finnish MPs says, trying to overturn parliament's negative stance on more nuclear capacity.
- U.S. investors have not shown great interest in Finnish markets, only 0.3 percent of investments in EU countries came to Finland. @
- Finnish European Parliament representative Paavo Vayrynen says he will not run for presidency in 2000, because he does not want to challenge Centre Party leader Esko Aho.
- Drinking water is said to be free of blue-green toxic algae, which has covered large parts of Finnish inland and coastal waters.
